Specificity Index Statistic

Source: R/specificity.index.R
specificity.index.Rd

specificity.index calculates the specificity index statistic (pSI) for every gene in every cell type/sample of an expression matrix. The pSI identifies genes enriched in specific cell populations across a large number of profiles, and correctly predicts in situ hybridization patterns for many cell types (Dougherty et al. 2010).

Usage

specificity.index(
  pSI.in,
  pSI.in.filter,
  bts = 50,
  p_max = 0.1,
  e_min = 0.3,
  hist = FALSE,
  SI = FALSE,
  hist_file = NULL
)

Arguments

pSI.in

data frame with expression values for genes in rows and samples or cell types in columns (replicate arrays already averaged, so one column per cell type).

pSI.in.filter

optional matched data frame (same genes and samples) with NA for any gene that should be excluded for a particular cell type.

bts

numeric. Number of resampled distributions to average for the permutation test.

p_max

numeric. Maximum p-value to calculate; genes with larger p-values are returned as NA.

e_min

numeric. Minimum expression value for a gene to be included. A value of 50 has been used for microarray studies and 0.3 for RNA-seq studies.

hist

logical. If TRUE, draw histograms of the sampled (null) and actual distributions of mean gene rank for each cell type on the current graphics device, one page per cell type. (Before pSI 1.2.0 these were written as PNG files into the working directory.)

SI

logical. If TRUE, return the specificity index (mean rank) itself instead of the pSI p-value.

hist_file

optional path to a PDF file. If supplied, the histograms are written there (one page per cell type) instead of to the current device, and hist is treated as TRUE.

Value

A data frame with the same row and column names as pSI.in. Each cell holds the pSI value (a p-value) of that gene for that cell type/sample, or NA if the gene was excluded (expression below e_min, filtered by pSI.in.filter, or p-value above p_max). With SI = TRUE the specificity index is returned instead of the p-value.

Details

For cell type 1 and gene \(n\), the specificity index is the mean, over the other \(m-1\) cell types \(k\), of the rank (among all genes) of the expression ratio of that gene between cell type 1 and cell type \(k\): $$SI_{n,1}= \frac{ \sum_{k=2}^m rank( \frac{ IP_{1,n} }{ IP_{k,n} }) }{m-1}$$ A low SI means the gene is highly enriched in cell type 1 relative to the others. The pSI is a p-value for the observed SI, obtained by comparing it with a null distribution of SI values computed from bts expression matrices resampled with replacement. To save time it is only calculated for genes whose p-value is below p_max; all other genes, and genes with expression below e_min or set to NA in pSI.in.filter, are returned as NA.

Because the null distribution is resampled, results vary slightly from run to run; call set.seed first for a reproducible result.

References

Dougherty JD, Schmidt EF, Nakajima M, Heintz N (2010). Analytical approaches to RNA profiling data for the identification of genes enriched in specific cells. Nucleic Acids Research 38(13):4218-4230. doi:10.1093/nar/gkq130

See also

pSI.list, pSI.count, candidate.overlap, fisher.iteration

Author

Xiaoxiao Xu, Alan B. Wells, David R. O'Brien, Arye Nehorai, Joseph D. Dougherty

Examples

##load sample expression matrix
data(sample.data)
##calculate specificity index on expression matrix
##(Normally for RNAseq data, and e_min of 0.3, microarrays: e_min= 50)
set.seed(1)
pSI.output <- specificity.index(pSI.in=sample.data$pSI.input, e_min=20)
head(pSI.output[rowSums(!is.na(pSI.output)) > 0, ])
#>         Amygdala.Young.Adulthood Cerebellum.Young.Adulthood
#> HS3ST1                        NA                 0.02097571
#> CYP26B1                       NA                 0.00108459
#> DBNDD1                        NA                         NA
#> FKBP4                         NA                 0.07943886
#> CAMKK1                        NA                         NA
#> PRKAR2B                       NA                         NA
#>         Cortex.Young.Adulthood Hippocampus.Young.Adulthood
#> HS3ST1                      NA                          NA
#> CYP26B1                     NA                          NA
#> DBNDD1                      NA                          NA
#> FKBP4                       NA                          NA
#> CAMKK1              0.02654505                          NA
#> PRKAR2B             0.06262613                          NA
#>         Striatum.Young.Adulthood Thalamus.Young.Adulthood
#> HS3ST1                        NA                       NA
#> CYP26B1                       NA                       NA
#> DBNDD1                        NA              0.007593712
#> FKBP4                         NA                       NA
#> CAMKK1                        NA                       NA
#> PRKAR2B                       NA                       NA

##histograms of the sampled and actual rank distributions, to a temporary PDF
pdf_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf")
pSI.output <- specificity.index(pSI.in=sample.data$pSI.input, e_min=20,
                                hist_file=pdf_file)
unlink(pdf_file)
